newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil extends losses at close.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil extends losses at close.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL
May (3rd pos) 1,289 rgt/tonne Feb (south) 1,345
Open/Hi/Low 1,298/1,298/1,287 Prev close 1,360
Prev settlement 1,299 * sellers prices

PALM OIL FUTURES - The market turned sluggish in late trading ahead of PORLA data after falling earlier on news of India's proposal of a raise in edible oil import duty and losses in Chicago soyoil. SGS's Feb 1-20 export data had no impact. Selling was seen as May futures fell below 1,300 ringgit.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Prices were marked down but falls were limited by good fundamentals and tight supply in near term.
The Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) is releasing the January stock/output/export figures on February 22.
Cargo surveyor SGS (M) Sdn Bhd estimated February 1-20 exports at 269,684 tonnes, which was within market expectations and had no impact on the market, traders said.
"There was still a lot of uncertainties about the Indian proposal. The big question is whether it will be approved," said one trader.
"Though it is a proposal, the market is reacting to it," the trader said. "Prices are falling for fear that India may reduce its buying."
On Wednesday, Indian Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra said he has proposed the import duty on edible oils be increased to 30 percent from 20 percent.

Traders said a higher import duty would make palm oil even more expensive as it is already holding a premium over other edible oils. "Secondly, the ringgit's strength against the dollar had also made it more expensive to buy local palm oil," the trader said.
"Deng's death has no impact on the market which was moved by other factors. Soyoil fell last night and palm oil just took the cue from there," said another trader.
But the trader said the fall could be temporary as prices were still high.
"The underlying fundamentals remain firm and any falls could not be major unless some bearish news emerge," the trader added.
Traders expect a tight supply in the near-term because output is likely to be low due to the seasonal low production months.
Among refined products, Mar RBD palm oil was offered at $565 a tonne FOB Malaysia, Apr at $557.50 and Apr/May/Jun at $552.50. Mar was traded at $565 and Apr at $558.
Mar RBD palm olein saw offers at $592.50, Apr at $585 and Apr/May/Jun at $580. Mar was traded at $590 and $588.50.
Mar RBD palm stearin was offered at $465 and Mar palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $310.
